milestones: Day 1‑2: Set up environment & master Python basics (syntax, data types, control flow)
Day 3‑4: Work with collections, functions, and modules – build small utilities
Day 5‑6: Intro to file I/O, error handling, and popular standard‑library modules
Day 7: Build a complete mini‑project that ties all concepts together

dailyTasks.title: Environment & Hello‑World
dailyTasks.description:
• Install Python 3.x and VS Code (or your preferred IDE)
• Verify installation with `python --version`
• Write and run a “Hello, World!” script
• Learn about comments, indentation, basic REPL usage
• Study literals, variables, and simple arithmetic
• Practice: solve 5 tiny math puzzles on https://www.w3resource.com/python-exercises/

dailyTasks.title: Control Flow & Simple Data Types
dailyTasks.description:
• Conditional statements (`if/elif/else`)
• Loops (`for`, `while`) and `range`
• Basic data types: `int`, `float`, `bool`, `str`
• String methods & formatting (f‑strings)
• Practice: implement a command‑line “guess the number” game

dailyTasks.title: Collections – Lists & Tuples
dailyTasks.description:
• Create, index, slice, and iterate over lists
• List methods (`append`, `pop`, `sort`, comprehensions)
• Immutable tuples and when to use them
• Mini‑exercise: read a CSV‑style string and compute column statistics

dailyTasks.title: Dictionaries, Sets & Functions
dailyTasks.description:
• Dictionaries: creation, lookup, iteration, `dict.get`
• Sets: uniqueness, basic operations (`union`, `intersection`)
• Define functions, default arguments, `*args`/`**kwargs`
• Scope & the `global` keyword
• Practice: build a phone‑book lookup using a dictionary

dailyTasks.title: Modules, Packages & File I/O
dailyTasks.description:
• Importing standard modules (`math`, `random`, `datetime`)
• Creating your own module and using `__name__ == "__main__"`
• Reading/writing text files with `with open(...) as f`
• CSV handling via `csv` module
• Exercise: write a script that logs daily expenses to a CSV file

dailyTasks.title: Error Handling & Intro to Popular Libraries
dailyTasks.description:
• Try/except blocks, catching specific exceptions
• Using `finally` and custom exception classes
• Quick tour of `requests` (HTTP) and `json` for API calls
• Exercise: fetch a public JSON API (e.g., OpenWeather) and display selected data

dailyTasks.title: Capstone Mini‑Project
dailyTasks.description:
• Choose one of the following (≈150‑200 lines total):
   1. **Todo CLI** – add, list, complete, and delete tasks saved in a JSON file.
   2. **Currency Converter** – fetch live rates via an API, store history, and allow conversions.
   3. **Simple Quiz Game** – load questions from a CSV, track score, and write results to a file.
• Apply all learned concepts: functions, modules, file I/O, error handling, and external libraries.
• Test thoroughly and write a short README describing usage.
• Celebrate completion!

successMetrics: Complete at least 90 % of the daily tasks (e.g., write and run the required scripts).
Score ≥ 80 % on the end‑of‑day quizzes hosted on https://www.w3resource.com/python-exercises/ (or similar).
Capstone project runs without errors and passes 3 self‑designed test cases.
Be able to explain each core concept in one sentence without referring to notes.
challenges: Procrastination – the 7‑day sprint can feel intense.
Overwhelm from new terminology and error messages.
Difficulty debugging without a solid troubleshooting routine.
Limited prior programming experience may slow down comprehension of abstract concepts.
plan.motivationalApproach:
Use the **Micro‑Win + Visual Progress** method:
1. **Micro‑Wins** – break every daily task into 2‑3 bite‑size sub‑tasks; tick each off on a habit‑tracker (e.g., Notion or a simple spreadsheet). The act of checking boxes releases dopamine and builds momentum.
2. **Public Commitment** – post a brief daily update on a platform you trust (Twitter, Discord, a study group). Social accountability raises the cost of skipping a day.
3. **Reward Stack** – after each completed day, give yourself a small, predefined treat (a coffee, 20‑minute walk, an episode of a favorite show). After the full week, plan a larger reward (a new book, a dinner out, or a hobby session).
4. **Reflection Loop** – spend 5 minutes each evening noting:
   * What was learned?
   * What blocked you?
   * One thing you’ll improve tomorrow.
   This turns challenges into data for the next day and reinforces a growth mindset.
5. **Visualization** – spend 2 minutes each morning visualizing yourself confidently writing Python code and completing the week’s milestone. Mental rehearsal primes the brain for actual performance.
By coupling concrete progress markers with emotional rewards and social accountability, motivation stays high throughout the intensive 7‑day learning sprint.

milestones: Milestone 1 – Foundations (Day 1): Understand the web stack, set up development environment, master HTML & basic CSS.
Milestone 2 – Interactivity & Styling (Day 2): Build responsive layouts, learn core JavaScript concepts, manipulate the DOM.
Milestone 3 – Full‑stack Mini‑Project (Day 3): Combine HTML, CSS, and JavaScript into a functional web app, deploy it, and review next‑step learning paths.

dailyTasks.title: Web Foundations & HTML
dailyTasks.description:
• Install VS Code, Git, Node.js, and a browser (Chrome/Firefox). 
• Watch a 30‑minute intro video on how the Internet works (client‑server, HTTP, DNS). 
• Follow a hands‑on tutorial to create a static page: structure with semantic HTML tags (header, nav, main, footer). 
• Practice: Build a personal‑profile page containing a heading, image, list of skills, and contact links.
• Quick Quiz: 10 flash‑card questions on HTML element purposes.

dailyTasks.title: CSS & Intro to JavaScript
dailyTasks.description:
• Review CSS basics: selectors, box model, display, positioning. 
• Follow a guided tutorial to style the Day‑1 profile page: typography, colors, flexbox layout, responsive breakpoints (mobile‑first). 
• Intro JavaScript (30‑min video + 2‑hour coding): variables, data types, functions, events, DOM manipulation. 
• Mini‑exercise: Add a “Show More / Show Less” button that toggles extra content on the profile page.
• Deploy the styled page to GitHub Pages (free static hosting).

dailyTasks.title: Mini Full‑Stack Project & Deployment
dailyTasks.description:
• Project Scope (2‑hour): Build a simple “To‑Do List” web app.
   - HTML: input field, add button, list container.
   - CSS: clean, responsive design using Flexbox/Grid.
   - JavaScript: add, delete, toggle‑complete items; persist data in localStorage.
• Step‑by‑step coding (follow a fast‑track tutorial, then refactor on your own). 
• Testing: verify functionality on desktop & mobile browsers.
• Deploy: push to GitHub, enable GitHub Pages, share the live URL.
• Reflection: Write a 200‑word summary of what you learned, what was hardest, and next topics (e.g., APIs, frameworks).

successMetrics: ✅ All three daily deliverables are completed and pushed to a public GitHub repository.
✅ The final mini‑project works offline, stores tasks in localStorage, and is responsive on both a phone and a desktop screen.
✅ Ability to explain, without reference, the purpose of HTML5 semantic tags, three CSS layout techniques (flexbox, grid, float), and basic JavaScript event handling.
challenges: Time pressure – 3 days is a sprint; fatigue can reduce retention.
Over‑whelm from the sheer amount of terminology (DOM, flexbox, Git, etc.).
Debugging without prior experience may stall progress.
Potential setup issues (Node.js, VS Code extensions, Git authentication).
plan.motivationalApproach: Use the **“micro‑wins”** technique: celebrate each completed task with a 2‑minute break, a quick stretch, or a small reward (e.g., a favorite snack). Pair the sprint with a **visual progress board** (Kanban columns: To‑Do → In‑Progress → Done) so you can see the wall shrink in real time. Leverage **accountability** – share your daily GitHub commits on a public channel or with a friend and invite brief feedback. Finally, remind yourself that 3 days will give you a **functional prototype**, not mastery; treat this as the first solid foothold on a much larger climbing wall, and plan a follow‑up learning cycle (e.g., React, Node/Express, APIs) once the sprint ends.
